text:
incident-bot: PAGER — INC-2026-342: Elevated 5xx rate detected in uk-west (uk-west-1) on /v1/generate. Error rate jumped 0.2% -> 6.8% over 3m. Autoscaling healthy. Paging SREs.

SRE Pager: paging @anya (oncall) and @mike (infra) — please ack.

anya: acked. I'm pulling traces and tail logs now. Seeing spike of 502s correlated with long-context model shards (redwood-long-v1). CPU and KV miss rate high on a subset of nodes.

mike: taking a look at provider telemetry. Provider-A fast path shows numerous 504/502s and higher p99 latency (~600ms). Provider-B looks healthy. We should consider a soft traffic shift + short-term quota/rate limits.

lucas: options: (A) immediate 30% reroute to provider-B; (B) staged bucketed weights (10% every 2m) to avoid cache churn. I prefer B.

anya: +1 for staged. Also propose a partial brownout: disable long-context model for new sessions in uk-west and fallback to redwood-base-v2. That should cut KV pressure. Can product ok this? @eva

eva: OK to disable long-context for new sessions in uk-west for the duration. Need CS to prep messaging.

zoe: I'll draft a short customer blurb: "We're temporarily restricting very-long context models in UK while we stabilize. Some long-history requests may fall back to shorter context models; no data lost. We expect restoration within ~1 hour." Will share template.

mike: executing soft quota adjustments now — reducing max concurrent streams for free tier in uk-west to 4 and applying route-level rate-limit multiplier 0.6. Command I ran:

```bash
# reduce free-tier concurrency in config-store
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/patch 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"route": "/v1/generate","region":"uk-west","overrides": {"free_tier.max_concurrency": 4, "rate_limit.multiplier": 0.6}}'
```

mike: also toggled model mapping for new sessions: redirect redwood-long-v1 -> redwood-base-v2 for uk-west (new session mapping only).

deploy-bot: rollout started: traffic-router/tr-2026-88 -> staged rollout to uk-west routing plane.

lucas: starting staged provider weight shift. Step 1: provider-A weight 0.90 -> 0.80, provider-B 0.10 -> 0.20. Applying now (will incrementally shift every 2m as discussed).

anya: monitoring metrics... errors dropping to 2.1% within 3 minutes of first actions. Latency p99 also trending down. Good signal.

mike: next scheduled shift in ~2m to bring A->0.70/B->0.30. I'll hold if we see any instability.

lucas: note — cache warmups might spike some tail latency for a minute after each bump. We'll watch.

anya: customer impact summary for now: ~12% of requests in uk-west see degraded quality (long-context fallback) and ~30% of traffic routed to provider-B; some non-critical increased latency during weight bumps. No data loss, no auth failures.

zoe: posted CS note to status draft channel, tagging enterprise reps for UK customers.

mike: second weight bump applied: A 0.80 -> 0.70. No regressions observed. Errors now ~0.9%.

anya: looks stable. I'm going to notify rotations: @oncall-night please standby for handoff in 15m in case we need overnight coverage.

eva: planning decision: keep long-context disabled for new sessions until at least one postmortem and a remediation plan (KV tuning / model shard redistribution).

deploy-bot: rollout completed for traffic-router/tr-2026-88.

anya: marking this mitigated for now. Moving to monitoring and postmortem. Will hand off to @mike as secondary oncall in 15m for follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-342 status -> mitigated (temporary controls in place: staged provider weights, rate-limit multiplier, free-tier concurrency cap, long-context fallback). Postmortem ticket INC-2026-342-PM created.

mike: I'll stay on rotation for next 30m and then hand off formally. Great coordination, everyone. :thumbsup:
